body:
`insight:capital-light-compounding` · confidence: verified

Cases: Monster (outsourced bottling + distributors; best US stock of 30 years, ~+200,000%), Costco (membership fees ~ most of profit; ~29x since 2009), Constellation Software (~300x via small VMS acquisitions funded by FCF), Domino's (franchise; ~180x from trough), Hermès (scarcity pricing; ~30x), Booking (agency model). Shared traits: high returns on incremental capital, someone else funds the assets (co-packers, franchisees, suppliers via negative working capital, customers via membership fees), long-tenured owner-managers (Sacks/Schlosberg, Munger's influence, Leonard, Dumas family), and EPS growth doing most of the work for a decade or more. Early signals: rising gross margin with flat capex, renewal/retention data, management letters reporting ROIC honestly. Where they stall: (1) key-person exit plus a new threat (Constellation -51% after Leonard left + AI fears); (2) the multiple gets ahead of growth (Costco ~50-60x on high-single-digit growth; Hermès ~50x before a ~-50% fall); (3) growth slows to GDP-plus (Monster 2022-24, Domino's 2022-26). Lesson: these are the best 'hold forever' candidates, but late-stage returns depend on entry multiple; a P/E doubling in the last stretch is a non-repeatable gift.

- **Links:** `case_study:monster-beverage-2002-2024`, `case_study:costco-2009-2026`, `case_study:constellation-software-2006-2026`, `insight:twin-engine`, `strategy:marcellus-cc`
- **Sources:** [1](https://www.cnbc.com/2024/02/17/monster-energy-drink-stock-is-best-performer-of-the-last-30-years.html) · [2](https://www.fool.com/investing/2025/01/11/heres-what-happened-the-last-time-costco-stock-was) · [3](https://betakit.com/constellation-software-shares-close-week-down-17-percent-after-founder-and-ceo-steps-down/)

`insight:abel-2025-capital-allocation-principles` | confidence: verified | date: 2026-02-28

Berkshire's 2025 letter (published 2026) is the first signed by Greg Abel as CEO; Buffett remains Chairman. Stated criteria, verbatim bullets: 'Invest in businesses that we thoroughly understand, with durable advantages and long-term economic prospects'; 'Partner with high integrity leaders who understand their customers and act like owners'; 'Avoid businesses that undermine the fabric of society or could jeopardize Berkshire's reputation'; 'Act quickly and concentrate our capital in a few high conviction ideas'; 'Maintain discipline and let compounding unfold.' Opportunities are judged on growth of 'intrinsic value per share over a time horizon measured in perpetuity.' Cash and US Treasuries 'now exceed $370 billion' - 'our dry powder' - and a large cash position 'does not' signal 'a retreat from investing.' 2025 deals: OxyChem (from Occidental) and Bell Laboratories (rodent control: 'easy to understand and always needed' - 'We only wish it had been ten times bigger'). Buybacks only 'below our estimate of intrinsic value, conservatively determined'; no dividend while $1 retained creates >$1 of value. Operating cash flow $46bn in 2025 vs >$40bn five-year average. Candour carried over: Kraft Heinz 'disappointing', Pilot control delay a 'mistake'. Actionable: a ready-made 5-line purchase checklist; patience with cash is a position, not a failure.

Sources:
- https://www.berkshirehathaway.com/letters/2025ltr.pdf

`insight:marks-something-of-value-2021` | confidence: verified | date: 2021-01-11

Memo of 11 Jan 2021, from months of debate with his son Andrew (a growth/tech investor) during the pandemic. Context: growth had beaten value for ~13 years. Conclusions: 'carrying low valuation parameters' is 'far from synonymous with "underpriced"'; 'a stock with a low p/e ratio, for example, is likely to be a bargain only if its current earnings and recent earnings growth are indicative of the future.' Pure low-multiple pursuit leads to 'value traps': things that look cheap 'because they have operating weaknesses or because the sales and earnings creating those valuations can't be replicated.' On edge: 'Since quantitative information regarding the present is so readily available, success in the highly competitive field of investing is more likely to be the result of superior judgments about qualitative factors and future events'; 'successful investing has to be more about superior judgments concerning (a) qualitative, non-computable factors and (b) how things are likely to unfold in the future.' Marks admits Oaktree's Graham-style caution may have cost returns in winners-take-most industries. Actionable: public screens (low P/E, high ROE on screener.in) carry no edge by themselves; edge comes from scuttlebutt, industry structure and variant perception about the future.

Sources:
- https://www.oaktreecapital.com/insights/memo/something-of-value

- **Top-minus-bottom (raw returns) is still strong:** 63d **+5.14%** [+2.81, +7.98], t 3.87; 21d +3.15% (t 4.5); 126d
  +5.88% (t 2.7, Dec-25 and part of Mar-26 only). The anomaly is alive in 2026 and about as large as in v1 (test
  +4.24%). Again, the money is mostly on the **short or avoid side**.
- **Quintile ladder, 63d excess:** Q1 −2.73, **Q2 −2.81**, Q3 −0.15, Q4 +1.43, Q5 +2.41%. The "avoid" zone covers the
  bottom two quintiles, not only the bottom one.
- **By quarter, top vs controls at 63d:** Dec-25 +0.87%, Mar-26 +1.85%, Jun-26 **+4.47%**. Bottom: −2.02, −4.20, −2.08%.
  The long leg is positive in all three quarters but carried by Jun-26. The bottom leg is negative in all three.
- **Consolidated-only events** (79%): top +2.63% (t 3.0), bottom −2.43% (t −3.2), close to the full set. Consolidated
  EPS did not obviously sharpen the signal compared with v1's standalone figures.
- **Calibration:** all events vs controls −0.37% at 63d (t −1.25), and −0.54% at 21d (t −2.3). The slight negative is
  probably the mechanical "single stock vs equal-weight mean of ~370 stocks" effect noted in v1. It works *against* the
  long leg, so it does not flatter it.
- **Sep-2026 quarter (filed Oct–Nov 2026): PENDING.** Its 21d windows close in late Nov–mid Dec 2026, and its 63d
  windows in Jan–Feb 2027. At the run date only 45 events had a closed 21d window, which is too few to report. Re-run
  `v2_events.py` + `v2_analyze.py` after about 2027-02-20.
- **The fresh result is close to a replica of v1's test result.** Gross long-only +2.41% (v1 +2.36%), net of 1%
  +1.41% with a CI touching zero (v1 +1.36%, CI −0.06). Two independent periods now give the same answer: a real
  but small long-only edge of about +2.4% per quarter gross. It is **not separable from zero once a 1% round trip is
  paid**, at 3–4 years' or 3 quarters' worth of data.

*(Stage 2, the 2022–25 re-run with consolidated EPS, is **PENDING**. The pass-B fetch of quarters Jun-2019 → Sep-2022 was still running at hand-off, so its numbers are not yet in this report. When pass B completes, run `v2_events.py V1 V2` then `v2_analyze.py V2` and add the RERUN block. H1 is already "not supported" because the fresh half failed, so the re-run cannot change the H1 verdict.)*

body:
- FY2025 company-level guidance was met: EPS $3.85 in a $3.70-3.90 band (narrowed to $3.70-3.85 in Oct), FCF $546 mn vs $500-525 mn, North America margin 24.4% in 24-24.5%, Rest of World 8.7% in 8-9%, buybacks $401 mn vs ~$400 mn (all XBRL-checked where tagged).
- The misses are China and sub-lines: FY2025 China -5..-8% (Jul) -> 'down 10%' (Oct) -> -12%; FY2025 capex $70.8 mn vs ~$75 mn.
- **FY2026 guidance was cut three times.** EPS $3.85-4.15 (Jan) -> $3.70-4.00 adjusted (Apr) -> $3.70-3.85 (Jul) -> $3.42-3.52 ex-China, continuing operations (Oct). Rest of World margin 8-9% -> 6-7%; water-treatment growth 10-12% -> 5-6% -> 3-4%; China 'mid-single-digit decline, growth in H2' -> 'low double digits' -> sold. Each cut was explicit and explained more than two quarters before the deadline, so clarification A scores them **withdrawn** (-0.5), not missed. Candour is high (7 of 8 shortfalls admitted unprompted).
- Leonard Valve: '~$70 mn of 2026 sales' (Jan, Jul) cut to $55 mn in Oct (final quarter: scored on outcome when FY2026 reports; 9M = $47 mn).
- The China sale (81% to CPE, $400 mn, close 'first half of 2027') is one of the calls. It changes the measurement basis of every FY2026 total-company promise: the calls use the ex-China, continuing-operations figures the company now guides.

body:
**NOT PROVEN by the pre-registered rule — direction confirmed, edge not.** Full-text cosine "changers" (bottom
quintile) earned **−7.3% vs size-matched controls over 12 months** (median −14.3%, hit rate 38%, naive t −2.53,
95% filing-month bootstrap CI **−14.1% to +1.0%**). The rule needed t ≤ −3 or a CI wholly below −0.5%; it got neither.
The shape matches the paper: almost nothing at 3 months (−0.6%), −1.3% at 6, −7.3% at 12 — slow drift, no reversal
in the window. The Jaccard version (secondary) was a bit stronger (−8.7%, t −3.08, CI −15.4 to +0.7).
**But about half the raw effect comes from one obvious group: first 10-Ks after a de-SPAC merger** (79 of 634
changers, 12%), where the "text change" is a whole new business and the stocks crashed in 2021–22. With de-SPACs
removed (exploratory), primary changers = −3.2% (CI −9.9 to +5.4). Removing biotech as well (an exploratory
sector-mix fix) brings it back to −7.2% (t −2.7) cosine / −9.5% (t −3.6) Jaccard. Those are post-hoc cuts, so they
are only hypotheses for a fresh test.
**Unexpected (secondary):** in Item 1A Risk Factors the effect ran *backwards*. Firms whose risk factors barely
changed did worst (−11.5% at 12 m, t −5.1). This survives removing de-SPACs and biotech (−10.6%, t −4.5), but it
contradicts the paper's strongest result and was not the hypothesis. Treat it as a new hypothesis ("stale,
copy-pasted risk factors") to test on fresh data, not as a finding.
title: lazy_prices_us › Verdict (short)

body:
- **Source:** annual reports are PDFs on NSE (corporate filings → annual reports) and BSE (AnnualReport archive).
  `tools/nse_fetch.py` / `tools/bse_fetch.py` don't fetch annual reports yet (an endpoint needs adding). `pdftotext`
  is installed here. Typical PDFs are 5–30 MB. Some are scanned and would need OCR (`pdftotext` returns little
  text for those, which is easy to detect).
- **Sections:** SEBI LODR Reg 34 / Schedule V requires an **MD&A** (including "risks and concerns") and a
  corporate-governance report. There is no standardised "Item 1A", so diff the MD&A plus the directors' report
  plus the auditor's report and CARO, and skip the financial statements.
- **Watch for template breaks:** BRSR became mandatory for the top 1,000 firms in FY2022-23, which creates a
  false "change" for every firm that year. Exclude BRSR pages, or diff with a section-aware parser.
- **Timing:** entry = the exchange submission date of the annual report (on or before the AGM notice), not the
  financial year end. Prices from Yahoo `.NS`, with the same size-matched-control method as the PEAD v2 work.
- **Cost:** roughly 1,500 firms × 2 years × ~10 MB ≈ 30 GB of downloads. That is too heavy for a sandbox session
  and belongs on the Pi pipeline (stage 1). A pilot of 200 firms × FY22→FY23→FY24 is feasible in one session.
